verdict.rationale: Greptile's first-party MCP server lets users drive it in plain language from their coding agent. Documented examples include prompts like "List unaddressed Greptile comments for PR #5 in owner/repo", fetching comments, applying fixes, managing patterns and reading the knowledge base; slash commands /check-pr and /greploop, written replies on review comments, and handing the onboarding page to an agent extend this. However, the natural-language layer is mostly supplied by the host agent rather than a native Greptile command interface, and core configuration (strictness, rules, triggers) is done through greptile.json or the dashboard. Missing for 10: native natural-language command interface within Greptile itself, natural-language control of configuration and settings, independent hands-on corroboration of the agent/MCP natural-language workflow.
